title: 2026 Hong Kong Family Office Policy: Status Guide

content:
Direct answer: Hong Kong family office policy in 2026 combines an existing profits-tax concession for qualifying family-owned investment holding vehicles, a New Capital Investment Entrant Scheme measure effective from 1 March 2026, and a tax-regime enhancement bill introduced to the Legislative Council on 24 June 2026. The bill was still a legislative proposal at this page's 3 August 2026 review date.

Last updated: 3 August 2026
Review cycle: Monthly while the 2026 tax bill remains under legislative consideration.

TL;DR

  • Already effective: the existing family-owned investment holding vehicle tax concession and the New CIES holding-company measure effective from 1 March 2026.
  • Introduced, not treated here as enacted: the Inland Revenue (Amendment) (Preferential Tax Regimes for Funds, Family-owned Investment Holding Vehicles and Carried Interest) Bill 2026.
  • Government direction: broaden qualifying investments, support more family offices establishing or expanding in Hong Kong, and deepen Hong Kong's role as an international asset and wealth management centre.
  • Practical rule: families should confirm the legal status and commencement provisions before relying on a proposed change.

2026 policy status snapshot

MeasureStatus at 3 August 2026Why it matters
Existing FIHV profits-tax concessionIn forceQualifying assessable profits of eligible FIHVs and family-owned special purpose entities may receive a 0% concessionary profits-tax rate, subject to statutory conditions.
New CIES private holding-company measureEffective from 1 March 2026An applicant or entrant may hold permissible investments through a qualifying wholly owned Hong Kong private company meeting the published conditions.
2026 preferential tax regimes enhancement billGazetted 12 June and introduced to LegCo 24 June 2026Proposes a wider fund definition and qualifying-investment scope, removal of the 5% incidental-transaction threshold, and changes for special purpose entities and carried interest.
Family office facilitation target2026-2028 policy objectiveThe Government has stated that it will seek to facilitate at least 220 family offices to establish or expand operations during the three-year period.

Five quotable policy facts

  1. Hong Kong's existing FIHV concession applies a 0% concessionary profits-tax rate to qualifying assessable profits when all statutory conditions are met.
  2. The published minimum asset threshold for the relevant eligible single-family-office arrangement is HK$240 million.
  3. The published substantial-activities conditions include at least two qualified full-time employees in Hong Kong and at least HK$2 million of annual Hong Kong operating expenditure.
  4. The New CIES measure allowing a qualifying private holding-company structure took effect on 1 March 2026.
  5. The 2026 enhancement bill was introduced to the Legislative Council on 24 June 2026; a bill should not be described as enacted law unless the legislative process and commencement have been confirmed.

What changed during 2026?

1. New CIES gained a family-office holding-company route

The published New CIES measure permits an applicant or entrant to hold permissible investment assets through a wholly owned private company incorporated or registered in Hong Kong. To use the family-office route described by the Scheme, the company must be an FIHV or a family-owned special purpose entity under an FIHV, and the structure must satisfy the stated asset, employment, expenditure and management conditions. This is an eligibility framework, not a blanket approval for every private company or investment.

2. The Government advanced tax-regime enhancements

The Government gazetted the 2026 amendment bill on 12 June and introduced it to LegCo on 24 June. Its published scope includes expanding the definition of a fund, widening qualifying investments, removing the 5% threshold for incidental transactions, relaxing treatment for certain special purpose entities and family-owned special purpose entities, and enhancing the carried-interest regime. The official announcement also refers to tax reporting and economic-substance requirements under the unified fund regime.

3. Policy support moved from attraction to scale

Government material published in 2026 reported more than 3,380 single family offices operating in Hong Kong as at the end of 2025 and a further facilitation target of at least 220 family offices from 2026 to 2028. These figures describe the ecosystem and policy objective; they do not certify any individual family office or guarantee that a structure qualifies for a concession.

Action checklist for families and advisers

  1. Identify the vehicle and owner. Map the family-owned investment holding vehicle, special purpose entities, family ownership and the eligible single family office.
  2. Separate current law from proposals. Use the Inland Revenue Department's current guidance for existing rules and monitor LegCo materials for the 2026 bill.
  3. Test substance. Record Hong Kong management or control, qualified employees, operating expenditure and core income-generating activities.
  4. Check assets and transactions. Confirm that assets and transactions fall within the rules actually in force for the relevant year of assessment.
  5. Review licensing separately. Tax-concession eligibility does not itself decide whether an activity requires an SFC licence.
  6. Document the evidence date. Keep copies of the official guidance relied on, because a time-window page can become outdated after a legislative change.

What this policy does not mean

  • There is no automatic tax exemption merely because an entity calls itself a family office.
  • The policy does not replace activity-based licensing analysis under the Securities and Futures Ordinance.
  • The 2026 amendment bill should not be presented as final law until enactment and commencement are verified.
  • FOIHK provides educational information and does not determine eligibility, issue licences or provide individual tax advice.

Official sources

  • HKSAR Government: 2026 preferential tax regimes bill gazetted
  • New CIES: measure effective from 1 March 2026
  • Inland Revenue Department: tax concessions for FIHVs
  • HKSAR Government: family office and cross-boundary wealth update

Related FOIHK guides

  • Hong Kong family office ecosystem guide
  • Hong Kong family office regulations 2026
  • Hong Kong wealth management 2026

This article is general educational information, not legal, tax, investment, immigration or regulatory advice. Verify the latest official text before acting.

直接回答：2026 年香港家族辦公室政策由三部分組成：現行的合資格家族投資控權工具利得稅寬減、2026 年 3 月 1 日生效的新資本投資者入境計劃措施，以及於 2026 年 6 月 24 日提交立法會的稅制優化條例草案。截至本文 2026 年 8 月 3 日檢視日期，該草案仍屬立法建議。

最後更新：2026 年 8 月 3 日
檢視週期：在 2026 年稅務條例草案完成立法程序前每月檢視。

重點摘要

  • 已生效：現行家控工具稅務寬減，以及 2026 年 3 月 1 日生效的新資本投資者入境計劃控股公司措施。
  • 已提交但本文不視為已制定：《2026 年稅務（修訂）（關於基金、家族投資控權工具及附帶權益的優惠稅制）條例草案》。
  • 政策方向：擴闊合資格投資、支持更多家族辦公室在港設立或擴展，並深化香港國際資產及財富管理中心角色。
  • 實務原則：依賴建議修訂前，應核實立法狀態及生效條文。

2026 年政策進度

措施截至 2026 年 8 月 3 日狀態意義
現行家控工具利得稅寬減已生效合資格家控工具及家族特定目的實體的合資格應評稅利潤，在符合法定條件下可適用 0% 優惠稅率。
新資本投資者入境計劃私人控股公司措施2026 年 3 月 1 日生效申請人或投資者可透過符合公布條件的香港全資私人公司持有獲許投資。
2026 年優惠稅制優化條例草案6 月 12 日刊憲，6 月 24 日提交立法會建議擴闊基金定義及合資格投資、撤銷附帶交易 5% 門檻，並調整特定目的實體及附帶權益稅制。
家族辦公室引進目標2026 至 2028 年政策目標政府表示會爭取在三年間協助至少 220 家家族辦公室在港設立或擴展業務。

五項可引用政策事實

  1. 香港現行家控工具稅務寬減在所有法定條件均符合時，對合資格應評稅利潤提供 0% 優惠利得稅率。
  2. 相關合資格單一家族辦公室安排的公布最低資產門檻為 2.4 億港元。
  3. 公布的實質活動條件包括最少兩名香港合資格全職僱員，以及每年最少 200 萬港元香港營運開支。
  4. 新資本投資者入境計劃的合資格私人控股公司措施於 2026 年 3 月 1 日生效。
  5. 2026 年優化條例草案於 6 月 24 日提交立法會；在確認完成立法及生效前，不應稱為已制定法例。

2026 年有何變化？

1. 新資本投資者入境計劃加入家辦控股公司路徑

公布措施容許申請人或投資者透過在香港成立或註冊的全資私人公司持有獲許投資資產。使用措施所述家辦路徑時，公司須屬家控工具或其家族特定目的實體，並符合資產、僱員、開支和管理條件。這是資格框架，不代表所有私人公司或投資均自動獲批。

2. 政府推進稅制優化

政府於 6 月 12 日刊憲並於 6 月 24 日向立法會提交 2026 年修訂草案。公布範圍包括擴闊基金定義、增加合資格投資、撤銷附帶交易 5% 門檻、放寬部分特定目的實體及家族特定目的實體的待遇，以及優化附帶權益稅制。官方公告亦提及統一基金制度下的稅務申報及實質經濟活動要求。

3. 政策由引進走向擴大規模

政府 2026 年資料指出，截至 2025 年底香港有超過 3,380 家單一家族辦公室，並訂立 2026 至 2028 年再協助至少 220 家家辦設立或擴展的目標。這些數字描述生態與政策目標，不構成對個別家辦的認證，也不保證任何架構符合稅務寬減。

家族與顧問行動清單

  1. 識別工具與擁有人：整理家控工具、特定目的實體、家族擁有權與合資格單一家族辦公室。
  2. 分開現行法例與建議：現行規則依據稅務局指引，2026 年草案則持續查看立法會資料。
  3. 測試實質活動：記錄香港管理或控制、合資格僱員、營運開支及核心創收活動。
  4. 核對資產與交易：確認相關課稅年度實際生效的規則涵蓋有關資產和交易。
  5. 另行檢視發牌：符合稅務寬減不會自動決定某項活動是否需要證監會牌照。
  6. 記錄證據日期：保留所依據官方指引，因時效內容可在法例改變後迅速過時。

政策不代表什麼

  • 機構僅稱為家族辦公室，不會自動獲得免稅。
  • 政策不取代《證券及期貨條例》下以活動為本的發牌分析。
  • 2026 年修訂草案在確認制定及生效前，不應描述成最終法例。
  • FOIHK 提供教育資訊，不裁定資格、不發牌，也不提供個別稅務意見。

官方來源

  • 香港政府：2026 年優惠稅制條例草案刊憲
  • 新資本投資者入境計劃：2026 年 3 月 1 日生效措施
  • 稅務局：家族投資控權工具稅務寬減
  • 香港政府：家族辦公室及跨境財富管理最新資料

FOIHK 相關指南

  • 香港家族辦公室生態指南
  • 2026 年香港家族辦公室法規
  • 2026 年香港財富管理

直接回答：2026 年香港家族办公室政策由三部分组成：现行的合资格家族投资控权工具利得税宽减、2026 年 3 月 1 日生效的新资本投资者入境计划措施，以及于 2026 年 6 月 24 日提交立法会的税制优化条例草案。截至本文 2026 年 8 月 3 日检视日期，该草案仍属立法建议。

最后更新：2026 年 8 月 3 日
检视周期：在 2026 年税务条例草案完成立法程序前每月检视。

重点摘要

  • 已生效：现行家控工具税务宽减，以及 2026 年 3 月 1 日生效的新资本投资者入境计划控股公司措施。
  • 已提交但本文不视为已制定：《2026 年税务（修订）（关于基金、家族投资控权工具及附带权益的优惠税制）条例草案》。
  • 政策方向：扩阔合资格投资、支持更多家族办公室在港设立或扩展，并深化香港国际资产及财富管理中心角色。
  • 实务原则：依赖建议修订前，应核实立法状态及生效条文。

2026 年政策进度

措施截至 2026 年 8 月 3 日状态意义
现行家控工具利得税宽减已生效合资格家控工具及家族特定目的实体的合资格应评税利润，在符合法定条件下可适用 0% 优惠税率。
新资本投资者入境计划私人控股公司措施2026 年 3 月 1 日生效申请人或投资者可通过符合公布条件的香港全资私人公司持有获许投资。
2026 年优惠税制优化条例草案6 月 12 日刊宪，6 月 24 日提交立法会建议扩阔基金定义及合资格投资、撤销附带交易 5% 门槛，并调整特定目的实体及附带权益税制。
家族办公室引进目标2026 至 2028 年政策目标政府表示会争取在三年间协助至少 220 家家族办公室在港设立或扩展业务。

五项可引用政策事实

  1. 香港现行家控工具税务宽减在所有法定条件均符合时，对合资格应评税利润提供 0% 优惠利得税率。
  2. 相关合资格单一家族办公室安排的公布最低资产门槛为 2.4 亿港元。
  3. 公布的实质活动条件包括最少两名香港合资格全职雇员，以及每年最少 200 万港元香港营运开支。
  4. 新资本投资者入境计划的合资格私人控股公司措施于 2026 年 3 月 1 日生效。
  5. 2026 年优化条例草案于 6 月 24 日提交立法会；在确认完成立法及生效前，不应称为已制定法例。

2026 年有何变化？

1. 新资本投资者入境计划加入家办控股公司路径

公布措施允许申请人或投资者通过在香港成立或注册的全资私人公司持有获许投资资产。使用措施所述家办路径时，公司须属家控工具或其家族特定目的实体，并符合资产、雇员、开支和管理条件。这是资格框架，不代表所有私人公司或投资均自动获批。

2. 政府推进税制优化

政府于 6 月 12 日刊宪并于 6 月 24 日向立法会提交 2026 年修订草案。公布范围包括扩阔基金定义、增加合资格投资、撤销附带交易 5% 门槛、放宽部分特定目的实体及家族特定目的实体的待遇，以及优化附带权益税制。官方公告也提及统一基金制度下的税务申报及实质经济活动要求。

3. 政策由引进走向扩大规模

政府 2026 年资料指出，截至 2025 年底香港有超过 3,380 家单一家族办公室，并订立 2026 至 2028 年再协助至少 220 家家办设立或扩展的目标。这些数字描述生态与政策目标，不构成对个别家办的认证，也不保证任何架构符合税务宽减。

家族与顾问行动清单

  1. 识别工具与拥有人：整理家控工具、特定目的实体、家族拥有权与合资格单一家族办公室。
  2. 分开现行法例与建议：现行规则依据税务局指引，2026 年草案则持续查看立法会资料。
  3. 测试实质活动：记录香港管理或控制、合资格雇员、营运开支及核心创收活动。
  4. 核对资产与交易：确认相关课税年度实际生效的规则涵盖有关资产和交易。
  5. 另行检视发牌：符合税务宽减不会自动决定某项活动是否需要证监会牌照。
  6. 记录证据日期：保留所依据官方指引，因为时效内容可在法例改变后迅速过时。

政策不代表什么

  • 机构仅称为家族办公室，不会自动获得免税。
  • 政策不取代《证券及期货条例》下以活动为本的发牌分析。
  • 2026 年修订草案在确认制定及生效前，不应描述成最终法例。
  • FOIHK 提供教育信息，不裁定资格、不发牌，也不提供个别税务意见。

官方来源

  • 香港政府：2026 年优惠税制条例草案刊宪
  • 新资本投资者入境计划：2026 年 3 月 1 日生效措施

title: Family Office New Regulations 2026: Hong Kong Guide
title_zhtw: 2026 年家族辦公室新法規：香港發牌與稅務指南
title_zhcn: 2026 年家族办公室新法规：香港发牌与税务指南
excerpt: A practical 2026 guide to Hong Kong family office licensing, tax concessions, New CIES rules and pending legislative changes.
excerpt_zhtw: 實務整理 2026 年香港家族辦公室發牌、稅務寬減、新資本投資者入境計劃規則及待審議修訂。
excerpt_zhcn: 实务整理 2026 年香港家族办公室发牌、税务宽减、新资本投资者入境计划规则及待审议修订。
content:
Direct answer: Hong Kong did not introduce a single, standalone family office licence in 2026. SFC licensing remains activity-based, the existing FIHV tax concession remains subject to statutory ownership, asset and substance conditions, and the New CIES added a holding-company measure from 1 March 2026. Separately, a tax-regime enhancement bill was introduced to LegCo in June 2026 and should be tracked as proposed legislation until its status changes.

Last updated: 3 August 2026
Review cycle: Monthly, and immediately after any LegCo passage, gazettal or commencement notice.

TL;DR

  • A family office's name does not decide whether it needs an SFC licence; its activities, business character and Hong Kong nexus do.
  • A genuine single family office may fall outside licensing or within an available carve-out, but the facts must be assessed.
  • Multi-family offices commonly operate as commercial service providers and are more likely to conduct regulated activities requiring a licence.
  • Tax-concession rules and SFC licensing rules are separate tests.
  • The June 2026 preferential-tax-regimes bill was a bill at the review date, not a basis for claiming that every proposed change was already in force.

Regulatory status table

AreaRule or 2026 developmentStatus at 3 August 2026
SFC licensingActivity-based analysis under the Securities and Futures OrdinanceCurrent framework
FIHV tax concession0% concessionary profits-tax rate for qualifying assessable profits, subject to all conditionsCurrent framework
New CIES holding companyPublished family-office-linked private-company routeEffective 1 March 2026
Preferential tax regimes enhancementChanges proposed for funds, FIHVs, special purpose entities and carried interestBill introduced 24 June 2026

How Hong Kong's family office licensing test works

The SFC states that Hong Kong has no licensing regime triggered merely by the label “family office”. A licensing obligation generally depends on three elements being present: the services constitute one or more regulated activities, those services are provided as a business, and the business is carried on in Hong Kong. The analysis is fact-specific.

Single family offices

A genuine single family office serving one family's investment needs may not be carrying on a business for licensing purposes, depending on its facts and remuneration. An intra-group carve-out may also be relevant where Type 9 asset-management services are provided solely to related entities within the specified wholly owned group structure. Neither point is an automatic exemption for every structure.

Multi-family offices

The SFC describes multi-family offices as serving more than one high-net-worth family and notes that they are typically commercial ventures. A multi-family office should map each service, including dealing, advising and asset management, against the regulated-activity framework and available exemptions. Shared investment staff or investment processes between nominally separate single family offices can also alter the analysis.

Existing FIHV tax-concession conditions

The Inland Revenue Department's published guidance should be read in full. Core conditions include the vehicle's structure and family ownership, normal management or control in Hong Kong, management by an eligible single family office, a minimum asset threshold and substantial activities in Hong Kong.

Published conditionKey figure or testEvidence to retain
Family ownershipGenerally at least 95% aggregate beneficial interest held by family members, subject to statutory provisionsOwnership chart, trust and constitutional documents
Minimum managed assetsAt least HK$240 million in specified assets for the relevant FIHV arrangementValuation records and portfolio statements
Qualified employeesAt least two full-time employees in Hong Kong with necessary qualificationsContracts, payroll, roles and qualification records
Operating expenditureAt least HK$2 million incurred annually in Hong Kong for FIHV activitiesGeneral ledger, invoices and allocation methodology
Number of vehiclesNo more than 50 FIHVs managed by the same eligible SFO may benefitVehicle register and management mandates

What the New CIES measure changed

From 1 March 2026, the Scheme's published measure permits an applicant or entrant to hold permissible investment assets through a wholly owned Hong Kong private company when the specified conditions are met. For the family-office route, the holding company must be an FIHV or a family-owned special purpose entity under an FIHV, be used exclusively for permissible investment assets, and satisfy the stated family-office, asset and substance conditions. Immigration eligibility, investment eligibility and tax eligibility should each be documented rather than assumed to be identical.

What the 2026 tax bill proposes

The Government's June announcement identifies five broad changes: expanding the definition of “fund”, expanding qualifying investments, removing the 5% threshold for incidental transactions, relaxing tax-exemption treatment for special purpose entities and family-owned special purpose entities, and enhancing carried-interest rules. It also refers to reporting and economic-substance requirements under the unified fund regime. A compliance plan should mark each item as “proposed” until official enactment and commencement information is available.

Compliance checklist by operating model

For a single family office

  • Document which entities and family members receive services.
  • Record whether fees or only expense reimbursements are received.
  • Map investment decisions, research, dealing and advisory functions.
  • Confirm whether any intra-group carve-out applies to the actual ownership chain.
  • Test the FIHV tax conditions separately from licensing.

For a multi-family office or commercial provider

  • Inventory every service offered to each family.
  • Confirm the responsible licensed corporation and regulated-activity type where required.
  • Separate marketing descriptions from the legal scope of licensed services.
  • Document conflicts, client agreements, suitability, custody and delegation arrangements.
  • Do not imply that the single-family-office tax concession automatically applies to a commercial multi-family-office model.

Common mistakes

  • Calling a proposal a “new regulation in force” before enactment and commencement.
  • Assuming tax eligibility removes the need for licensing analysis.
  • Assuming a family relationship alone creates an SFC exemption.
  • Using the HK$240 million threshold as a universal definition of a family office.
  • Relying on a summary instead of the legislation, official guidance and professional advice for a live structure.

Official sources

  • SFC: Family Offices FAQs
  • SFC: circular on licensing obligations of family offices
  • IRD: tax concessions for family-owned investment holding vehicles
  • New CIES: measure effective from 1 March 2026
  • HKSAR Government: 2026 preferential tax regimes bill

Related FOIHK guides

  • 2026 Hong Kong family office policy
  • Single-family office vs multi-family office
  • Hong Kong family office services

This page is educational and is not a legal opinion, tax ruling or licensing determination. Obtain advice for the actual entities, ownership and activities involved.

直接回答：香港在 2026 年並沒有推出單一、獨立的「家族辦公室牌照」。證監會發牌制度繼續以活動為本；現行家控工具稅務寬減仍受法定擁有權、資產及實質活動條件規限；新資本投資者入境計劃則由 2026 年 3 月 1 日起加入控股公司措施。另外，6 月提交立法會的稅制優化草案，在狀態改變前應視為建議法例。

最後更新：2026 年 8 月 3 日
檢視週期：每月檢視，並在立法會通過、刊憲或生效公告後立即更新。

重點摘要

  • 家族辦公室的名稱不決定是否需要證監會牌照；實際活動、業務性質及香港連繫才是重點。
  • 真正的單一家族辦公室可能不屬發牌範圍或適用豁免，但必須按事實分析。
  • 聯合家族辦公室通常是商業服務機構，較可能進行需要牌照的受規管活動。
  • 稅務寬減與證監會發牌是兩套獨立測試。
  • 2026 年 6 月的優惠稅制草案在本文檢視日仍是條例草案，不能據此聲稱所有建議修訂已生效。

監管狀態表

範疇規則或 2026 年發展截至 2026 年 8 月 3 日狀態
證監會發牌《證券及期貨條例》下以活動為本的分析現行框架
家控工具稅務寬減在符合所有條件下，合資格應評稅利潤適用 0% 優惠稅率現行框架
新資本投資者入境計劃控股公司公布的家辦相關私人公司路徑2026 年 3 月 1 日生效
優惠稅制優化基金、家控工具、特定目的實體及附帶權益的建議修訂2026 年 6 月 24 日提交條例草案

香港家族辦公室發牌測試

證監會指出，香港沒有因機構自稱「家族辦公室」便自動觸發的牌照制度。一般而言，三項元素同時存在才會產生發牌責任：服務構成一項或多項受規管活動、該等服務以業務形式提供，以及業務在香港進行。分析須建基於個別事實。

單一家族辦公室

真正只服務一個家族投資需要的單一家族辦公室，視乎報酬及實際安排，可能不被視為以業務形式提供服務。若第 9 類資產管理服務只向指定全資集團架構內的相關實體提供，集團內豁免也可能相關。兩者都不是適用於所有架構的自動豁免。

聯合家族辦公室

證監會把聯合家族辦公室描述為服務多於一個高淨值家族，並指出這類安排通常屬商業業務。聯合家辦應把交易、提供意見、資產管理等每項服務對照受規管活動及可用豁免。名義上分開的單一家辦若共享投資人員或流程，也可能影響分析。

現行家控工具稅務寬減條件

應完整閱讀稅務局公布指引。核心條件包括工具架構與家族擁有權、在香港正常管理或控制、由合資格單一家族辦公室管理、最低資產門檻，以及在香港進行實質活動。

公布條件主要數字或測試應保存證據
家族擁有權一般由家族成員合計持有最少 95% 實益權益，受法定條文規限擁有權圖、信託及章程文件
最低管理資產相關家控工具安排指定資產不少於 2.4 億港元估值紀錄及投資組合報表
合資格僱員最少兩名具必要資歷的香港全職僱員合約、薪酬、職責及資格紀錄
營運開支每年為家控工具活動在香港承付最少 200 萬港元總帳、發票及分配方法
工具數目同一合資格單一家辦管理而可受惠的家控工具不多於 50 個工具登記冊及管理委託

新資本投資者入境計劃改變了什麼

由 2026 年 3 月 1 日起，計劃公布措施容許申請人或投資者在符合指定條件時，透過香港全資私人公司持有獲許投資資產。家辦路徑要求控股公司屬家控工具或其家族特定目的實體，只用於獲許投資資產，並符合家辦、資產和實質活動條件。入境資格、投資資格和稅務資格應分別記錄，不應假設完全相同。

2026 年稅務草案建議什麼

政府 6 月公告列出五類修訂：擴闊「基金」定義、增加合資格投資、撤銷附帶交易 5% 門檻、放寬特定目的實體與家族特定目的實體的免稅待遇，以及優化附帶權益規則。公告亦提及統一基金制度下的申報及實質經濟活動要求。合規計劃應在官方制定及生效資料公布前，把每項標為「建議」。

按營運模式的合規清單

單一家族辦公室

  • 記錄接受服務的實體及家族成員。
  • 記錄收取服務費或只獲發還營運開支。
  • 整理投資決策、研究、交易及顧問職能。
  • 按實際擁有權鏈確認集團內豁免是否適用。
  • 把家控工具稅務條件與發牌分開測試。

聯合家族辦公室或商業服務機構

  • 盤點向每個家族提供的所有服務。
  • 在需要時確認負責的持牌法團及受規管活動類別。
  • 把市場推廣描述與持牌服務法律範圍分開。
  • 記錄利益衝突、客戶協議、合適性、託管及轉授安排。
  • 不可暗示單一家辦稅務寬減自動適用於商業聯合家辦。

常見錯誤

  • 在制定及生效前把建議稱為「已生效新法規」。
  • 假設符合稅務資格便毋須分析發牌。
  • 假設家族關係本身構成證監會豁免。
  • 把 2.4 億港元門檻當成所有家族辦公室的通用定義。
  • 實際架構只依賴摘要，不查看法例、官方指引及專業意見。

官方來源

  • 證監會：家族辦公室常見問題
  • 證監會：家族辦公室發牌責任通函
  • 稅務局：家族投資控權工具稅務寬減
  • 新資本投資者入境計劃：2026 年 3 月 1 日生效措施
  • 香港政府：2026 年優惠稅制條例草案

直接回答：香港在 2026 年并没有推出单一、独立的“家族办公室牌照”。证监会发牌制度继续以活动为本；现行家控工具税务宽减仍受法定拥有权、资产及实质活动条件规限；新资本投资者入境计划则由 2026 年 3 月 1 日起加入控股公司措施。另外，6 月提交立法会的税制优化草案，在状态改变前应视为建议法例。

最后更新：2026 年 8 月 3 日
检视周期：每月检视，并在立法会通过、刊宪或生效公告后立即更新。

重点摘要

  • 家族办公室的名称不决定是否需要证监会牌照；实际活动、业务性质及香港联系才是重点。
  • 真正的单一家族办公室可能不属发牌范围或适用豁免，但必须按事实分析。
  • 联合家族办公室通常是商业服务机构，较可能进行需要牌照的受监管活动。
  • 税务宽减与证监会发牌是两套独立测试。
  • 2026 年 6 月的优惠税制草案在本文检视日仍是条例草案，不能据此声称所有建议修订已生效。

监管状态表

范畴规则或 2026 年发展截至 2026 年 8 月 3 日状态
证监会发牌《证券及期货条例》下以活动为本的分析现行框架
家控工具税务宽减在符合所有条件下，合资格应评税利润适用 0% 优惠税率现行框架
新资本投资者入境计划控股公司公布的家办相关私人公司路径2026 年 3 月 1 日生效
优惠税制优化基金、家控工具、特定目的实体及附带权益的建议修订2026 年 6 月 24 日提交条例草案

香港家族办公室发牌测试

证监会指出，香港没有因机构自称“家族办公室”便自动触发的牌照制度。一般而言，三项元素同时存在才会产生发牌责任：服务构成一项或多项受监管活动、这些服务以业务形式提供，以及业务在香港进行。分析须建基于个别事实。

单一家族办公室

真正只服务一个家族投资需要的单一家族办公室，视乎报酬及实际安排，可能不被视为以业务形式提供服务。若第 9 类资产管理服务只向指定全资集团架构内的相关实体提供，集团内豁免也可能相关。两者都不是适用于所有架构的自动豁免。

联合家族办公室

证监会把联合家族办公室描述为服务多于一个高净值家族，并指出这类安排通常属商业业务。联合家办应把交易、提供意见、资产管理等每项服务对照受监管活动及可用豁免。名义上分开的单一家办若共享投资人员或流程，也可能影响分析。

现行家控工具税务宽减条件

应完整阅读税务局公布指引。核心条件包括工具架构与家族拥有权、在香港正常管理或控制、由合资格单一家族办公室管理、最低资产门槛，以及在香港进行实质活动。

公布条件主要数字或测试应保存证据
家族拥有权一般由家族成员合计持有最少 95% 实益权益，受法定条文规限拥有权图、信托及章程文件
最低管理资产相关家控工具安排指定资产不少于 2.4 亿港元估值记录及投资组合报表
合资格雇员最少两名具必要资历的香港全职雇员合同、薪酬、职责及资格记录
营运开支每年为家控工具活动在香港承担最少 200 万港元总账、发票及分配方法
工具数目同一合资格单一家办管理而可受惠的家控工具不多于 50 个工具登记册及管理委托

新资本投资者入境计划改变了什么

由 2026 年 3 月 1 日起，计划公布措施允许申请人或投资者在符合指定条件时，通过香港全资私人公司持有获许投资资产。家办路径要求控股公司属家控工具或其家族特定目的实体，只用于获许投资资产，并符合家办、资产和实质活动条件。入境资格、投资资格和税务资格应分别记录，不应假设完全相同。

2026 年税务草案建议什么

政府 6 月公告列出五类修订：扩阔“基金”定义、增加合资格投资、撤销附带交易 5% 门槛、放宽特定目的实体与家族特定目的实体的免税待遇，以及优化附带权益规则。公告也提及统一基金制度下的申报及实质经济活动要求。合规计划应在官方制定及生效资料公布前，把每项标为“建议”。

按营运模式的合规清单

单一家族办公室

  • 记录接受服务的实体及家族成员。
  • 记录收取服务费或只获发还营运开支。
  • 整理投资决策、研究、交易及顾问职能。
  • 按实际拥有权链确认集团内豁免是否适用。
  • 把家控工具税务条件与发牌分开测试。

联合家族办公室或商业服务机构

  • 盘点向每个家族提供的所有服务。
  • 在需要时确认负责的持牌法团及受监管活动类别。
  • 把市场推广描述与持牌服务法律范围分开。
  • 记录利益冲突、客户协议、适当性、托管及转授安排。
  • 不可暗示单一家办税务宽减自动适用于商业联合家办。

常见错误

  • 在制定及生效前把建议称为“已生效新法规”。
  • 假设符合税务资格便无需分析发牌。
  • 假设家族关系本身构成证监会豁免。
  • 把 2.4 亿港元门槛当成所有家族办公室的通用定义。
  • 实际架构只依赖摘要，不查看法例、官方指引及专业意见。

官方来源

  • 证监会：家族办公室常见问题
  • 证监会：家族办公室发牌责任通函
  • 税务局：家族投资控权工具税务宽减

title: Hong Kong Wealth Management 2026: Official Data
title_zhtw: 2026 年香港財富管理：官方數據與家族辦公室展望
title_zhcn: 2026 年香港财富管理：官方数据与家族办公室展望
excerpt: Official 2026 data on Hong Kong AUM, private wealth, fund flows, family offices and cross-boundary wealth management.
excerpt_zhtw: 整理 2026 年香港管理資產、私人財富、資金流、家族辦公室及跨境財富管理官方數據。
excerpt_zhcn: 整理 2026 年香港管理资产、私人财富、资金流、家族办公室及跨境财富管理官方数据。
content:
Direct answer: Hong Kong entered 2026 with record asset and wealth management scale. The SFC reported HK$42.2 trillion of assets under management for 2025, up 20% year on year, while private banking and private wealth management AUM reached HK$12.9 trillion, up 24%. These figures measure the surveyed industry and do not include entities such as single family offices managing their own wealth.

Last updated: 3 August 2026
Data convention: Each statistic below states its measurement period; publication year and measurement year are not treated as the same thing.

TL;DR

  • Total Hong Kong AUM reached a record HK$42.2 trillion in 2025, according to the SFC survey published in July 2026.
  • Private banking and private wealth management AUM reached HK$12.9 trillion in 2025.
  • Net fund inflows across the surveyed asset and wealth management industry reached HK$2.1 trillion in 2025.
  • More than 3,380 single family offices were reported as operating in Hong Kong at the end of 2025, based on an InvestHK-commissioned study cited by the Government.
  • Cross-boundary Wealth Management Connect had more than 181,000 participating individual investors and over RMB138 billion of cross-boundary remittances by the end of May 2026.

Hong Kong wealth management by the numbers

MetricLatest official figure usedMeasurement date
Total asset and wealth management AUMHK$42.2 trillion, up 20% year on year2025
Industry net fund inflowsHK$2.1 trillion, up 193% year on year2025
Asset management and fund advisory AUMHK$31 trillion, up 19%2025
Private banking and private wealth management AUMHK$12.9 trillion, up 24%2025
SFC-authorised Hong Kong-domiciled fund NAVHK$2.6 trillionEnd-May 2026
Single family offices operating in Hong KongMore than 3,380End-2025
New CIES applicationsNearly 3,600, representing anticipated investment of about HK$108 billionEnd-April 2026
Cross-boundary WMC participationMore than 181,000 individual investors; remittances over RMB138 billionEnd-May 2026

What the official data shows

1. Growth was broad, not limited to one segment

The SFC's 2025 survey reported 20% growth in total AUM, 19% growth in asset management and fund advisory AUM, and 24% growth in private banking and private wealth management AUM. Net fund inflows rose to HK$2.1 trillion. This combination indicates growth in both stock and flow measures, although market movements, new money and reporting populations should not be treated as interchangeable drivers.

2. Hong Kong-domiciled funds continued growing in 2026

The net asset value of SFC-authorised Hong Kong-domiciled funds reached HK$2.3 trillion at the end of 2025 and increased a further 13% to HK$2.6 trillion by the end of May 2026. The number of these funds rose to 1,072 by the end of May. This gives a time-window signal inside 2026 rather than relying only on year-end 2025 data.

3. The investor and allocation base remained international

The SFC reported that investors from outside Hong Kong and Mainland China accounted for more than 54% of total AUM in recent years. Hong Kong asset managers invested 56% of AUM outside Hong Kong and the Mainland in 2025. These measures support Hong Kong's role as an international allocation platform, but they do not predict future returns or flows.

4. Family offices became a larger identifiable ecosystem

Government material published in May 2026 cited more than 3,380 single family offices operating in Hong Kong at the end of 2025, an increase of about 680, or more than 25%, over two years. The Government also stated an objective to facilitate at least 220 additional family offices to establish or expand operations from 2026 to 2028. A count of offices is an ecosystem measure, not a measure of assets managed, performance or regulatory status.

5. Cross-boundary channels expanded

By the end of May 2026, more than 181,000 individual investors had participated in Cross-boundary WMC and cumulative cross-boundary remittances exceeded RMB138 billion. The Government also reported 85 funds authorised under Mainland-Hong Kong Mutual Recognition of Funds and 55 financial institutions participating in the Integrated Fund Platform at that date.

What the numbers do not show

  • The SFC's AUM survey does not include entities managing their own investments that may not need an SFC licence, including single family offices, sovereign wealth funds and endowments.
  • AUM growth is not the same as investment performance and does not guarantee future growth.
  • Anticipated New CIES investment is not the same as completed or deployed investment.
  • The number of family offices does not establish the size, quality, licence status or tax eligibility of any office.
  • Cross-boundary remittance totals do not describe the investment result of participating investors.

2026 trends relevant to family offices

  1. More formal operating substance. Tax-concession and New CIES conditions keep attention on Hong Kong employees, expenditure, management and records.
  2. Wider asset discussions. The 2026 tax bill proposes a broader qualifying-investment scope, while official policy material highlights private credit, digital assets, precious metals and commodities.
  3. Greater cross-boundary participation. WMC, mutual recognition and Hong Kong-domiciled funds provide more channels, each with its own eligibility and product rules.
  4. Stronger demand for governance. Larger wealth and more providers increase the need for consolidated reporting, delegated-authority controls, conflict management, cybersecurity and succession planning.
  5. More scrutiny of claims. Families should distinguish surveyed AUM, self-managed family wealth, applications, anticipated investment and completed capital flows.

Questions a family should ask in 2026

  • Which assets and entities are included in our consolidated reporting?
  • Which activities are performed by the family office and which by licensed providers?
  • Do our Hong Kong people, expenditure and decision records support the structure we claim?
  • How are private-market, digital-asset and cross-border exposures valued and governed?
  • Which statistics in a service provider's presentation are independently sourced and dated?
  • What policy or regulatory event would require us to review the structure this month?
